adopt_command_surface.replay_observation: adopt uses the same mutate()/replay rule as post: an existing message_id with identical content returns the existing row, with different content is refused (adapter l.245-269). From the CLI, observed_at is always a fresh timestamp (adapter l.810) and there is no flag to supply it, so re-running the same adopt command with the same --message-id was refused with `message_id already exists with different content` (A2, exit 1), even though every flag was identical. A gate or launcher that retries adopt with a fixed --message-id should expect exit 1 on the retry, not an idempotent success. Whether this is intended is not established.

post_refuses_adoption.behaviour: post --kind adoption is refused before any write: `kind adoption is written only by the `adopt` subcommand, not `post`` (exit 1)
post_refuses_adoption.mechanism: registry lookup of the kind's writer attribute (default 'post'), not a hard-coded exception
post_refuses_adoption.source: adapter l.307-312; registry l.59; behavioural P1
post_refuses_adoption.gate_recognition: The gate still recognises an adoption row by its fields (kind, topic, data.handoff_sha256, data.predecessor_session; plan l.739-746), not by which command wrote it. The row records no writer/command field (behavioural A1).
post_refuses_adoption.narrow_permission_command: `adopt` is the narrow command a host permission rule could allow for point 2 without allowing the broad `post`. This campaign writes no permission rule and does not claim one exists.

d10_delivery_by_to.current_wait_behaviour_observed: wait --topic session:<id> matched by exact topic only at this HEAD; the result has no matches/matched_by key (behavioural W1; keys: status, revision, messages, next_since, has_more, exclude_session_id, topics, topic). Exit 2 on timeout (W2; adapter l.774-775).
d10_delivery_by_to.reissue_contents: post-S2 adapter digest and the matches/matched_by result key
d10_delivery_by_to.s2_s5_integration_condition: Under D10, wait --topic session:X can return a row addressed to session:X on another topic. The gate must not rely on the S2 wait until its adoption recognition checks that the row's actual topic is session:<successor>, not only recipient plus digest. The gate's test on S2's integration fixture must show such a row is not accepted; that test is the gate owner's to write and run, and until it passes the gate keeps the HEAD wait behaviour (plan l.696-710).

three_questions.1_schema_validity: Answered by this note: the checks above are what a row must pass.
three_questions.2_host_permission: Whether the successor's host lets it run the board write at all (tool permission or sandbox). The gate owner's to establish; not implied by schema validity.
three_questions.3_authority_to_transfer_responsibility: User-open Q1. A schema-valid adoption establishes neither 2 nor 3, and the schema does not resolve Q1 (plan l.711-722; l.47-48).
three_questions.authentication: adopt authenticates no one: session_id is caller-supplied (plan l.133).

x6_closure_criterion.criterion: X6 closes only when adopt succeeds through a real Claude successor launched by the gate's launcher, under the intended permission configuration (whose grant needs the user's authorization, pending), with the host's actual rule-matching on the adopt command line tested in that run, and with --handoff-path passed; --handoff-sha256 alone does not count. A shell-stub test does not close it. The run and its record belong to the gate owner (S5).
